items.title: US Department of Labor proposes to modernize permanent labor certification recruitment, strengthening protections for American workers
items.summary: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today issued a proposed rule that would enhance American worker protections when employers apply for certification to hire foreign workers permanently in the United States. The proposed rule modernizes the Permanent Labor Certification program by strengthening recruitment standards and recordkeeping requirements, eliminating administrative exemptions to the statutory labor market test, and improving safeguards for all American workers, especially those affected by layoffs. This proposed update to the PERM program – the first comprehensive set of regulatory reforms to the program in nearly 20 years – will ensure that highly qualified American workers receive fair consideration and first access to job opportunities.“American Workers are the best in the world, and they deserve the first and best job opportunities. items.title: US Labor Department cites New Jersey pastry maker, staffing agency for endangering workers after 2 injuries in 3 months; proposes $351K in fines
items.summary: PEDRICKTOWN, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a pastry manufacturer and a staffing agency for endangering employees by exposing them to hazardous energy and amputation hazards.Investigators with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to an April 28 incident at Banneton Bakery LLC and found that an employee provided to the bakery by Idalia’s Staffing Agency was cleaning a moving conveyor belt when their arm got stuck, requiring medical treatment.During the investigation into the April 2026 incident, OSHA learned of a similar event that occurred on Jan. 16, 2026, in which an employee was cleaning the same conveyor belt and suffered a broken arm because the machinery was not locked out during the cleaning.The agency cited Banneton for two willful violations for failing to develop and use lockout/tagout procedures and failing to provide adequate training to ensure employees understood the purpose and function of energy control programs. items.title: US Department of Labor cites powder coating company for willful toxic substance exposures, repeat violations, proposes more than $1.6M in penalties
items.summary: HOUSTON – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a powder coating and furniture restoration company for willfully and repeatedly exposing workers to toxic substances and other safety and health hazards.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration conducted three inspections of Outdoor Furniture Refinishing Inc. – doing business as Allied Powder Coating – on April 10, 2026. One inspection addressed complaint items after the employer provided an inadequate response to an inquiry, and two follow-up inspections were initiated in relation to safety and health violations found during a December 2023 inspection. The employer’s failure to submit abatement documentation prompted a comprehensive review of ongoing hazards.OSHA cited the company for three willful violations for exposing workers to hazardous levels of 1,3,5-triglycidyl isocyanurate and total dust during powder coating operations. items.title: Amazon workers in Canada win first union contract in North America
items.summary: About 800 Amazon workers at the company’s YVR2 fulfilment centre in Delta, British Columbia, are now covered by the first binding collective agreement for Amazon workers anywhere in North America, after an independent arbitrator set its terms on Friday. The post Amazon workers in Canada win first union contract in North America appeared first on UNI Global Union .

items.title: US Department of Labor applauds federal appeals court decision on administrative exhaustion requirement under federal benefits law
items.summary: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor applauded a federal appeals court decision allowing employees to bring legal claims directly to federal court if they reasonably suspect fiduciary violations in their employee benefit plans covered under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act.Issued Oct. 13 by the en banc 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, the unanimous decision in Bolton v. Inland Fresh Seafood overturns precedent that required employees to exhaust all administrative remedies under their ERISA-covered employee benefit plans before they could go to federal court. “This decision vindicates the department’s reinvigorated amicus program and its focus on statutory text,” said Solicitor of Labor Jonathan Berry. “ERISA neither explicitly nor implicitly requires hard-working Americans to go anywhere but federal court to vindicate their statutory rights under it.
